sessions.title: Welcome to My Conference
sessions.description: A short hello from the organizers: what to expect over the next two days, where to find everything, and how to make the most of the event.

sessions.title: Opening Keynote: Build Less, Ship More
sessions.description: Why the best product teams delete more code than they write. A tour of lessons from a decade of shipping apps, with concrete habits you can adopt on Monday.

sessions.title: Design Systems That Survive Their Second Year
sessions.description: Most design systems die quietly after launch. This talk covers governance, versioning, and the social contracts that keep a component library alive.

sessions.title: Profiling for Humans
sessions.description: Flame graphs don't have to be scary. A practical walkthrough of finding and fixing the three performance problems almost every app has.

sessions.title: Offline First by Default
sessions.description: Networks fail on conference Wi-Fi and everywhere else. How to design data flows that treat connectivity as an enhancement, not a requirement.

sessions.title: Panel: Small Teams, Big Apps
sessions.description: Three engineers from very different companies compare notes on shipping and maintaining large apps with teams of fewer than five people.

sessions.title: Accessibility Is a Feature, Not a Checklist
sessions.description: Real stories from user testing with assistive technologies, and the small engineering habits that make apps genuinely usable for everyone.

sessions.title: Welcome Reception
sessions.description: Drinks, snacks, and good conversation in the lobby. Everyone is welcome.

sessions.title: Day 2 Keynote: The Boring Technology Club
sessions.description: Choosing proven tools is a superpower. A love letter to boring technology, and a framework for deciding when the shiny new thing is actually worth it.

sessions.title: Workshop: Testing the Untestable
sessions.description: Bring your laptop. We take a gnarly legacy screen with no tests and, step by step, make it safe to change. Seams, fakes, and when snapshot tests actually help.

sessions.title: Lightning Talks
sessions.description: Five talks, five minutes each, zero mercy from the countdown timer. Topics picked by the audience on day one.

sessions.title: Shipping With Confidence: Release Trains and Feature Flags
sessions.description: How to go from scary quarterly releases to calm weekly ones. Rollout strategies, kill switches, and the metrics that tell you when to stop a release.

sessions.title: The Art of the Empty State
sessions.description: First launches, no results, and error screens are where apps feel most human — or most broken. A designer's guide to the screens nobody prioritizes.

sessions.title: Closing Remarks & Community Awards
sessions.description: A wrap-up of the two days, thank-yous, and awards for the community projects that made this year special.

speakers.bio: Maya has shipped consumer apps for twelve years, most recently as a principal engineer at Orbital Labs. She writes about pragmatic engineering and keeps a running list of code she was glad to delete.
Sam is one of the organizers of My Conference and an engineering manager at Pinefield. They care deeply about community events and hallway-track conversations.
Tove leads design systems at Cobalt Apps. Before that she spent five years as a product designer on tooling teams, and she still prototypes everything in code first.
Devon is a staff engineer at Meridian Health, where a three-person team maintains an app used by millions of patients. Performance budgets are his love language.
Lena builds sync engines at Fernweh, a travel app that has to work in airplane mode by definition. She has strong opinions about retry logic and stronger ones about conflict resolution.
Priya is an accessibility engineer at Lumen Studio and a regular at local meetups. She runs usability sessions with assistive-technology users for every feature her team ships.
Jonas is the CTO of Brightside, a fintech startup that runs on deliberately boring technology. He previously spent a decade in infrastructure teams at larger companies.
